title: mistralai/Timestral-209M model card
note: 209M-parameter zero-shot forecasting model, largest of four sizes (5M, 28M, 123M, 209M). Takes past-only and known-future covariates, numeric or categorical. Context up to 32,768 steps, up to 1,024 steps per pass, 21 quantiles. Licence shown as Modified MIT. Runs on CPU or GPU via the timestral package. Training data and release date not stated; tech report marked coming soon.

title: mistralai/Timestral-209M model card
note: Vendor-reported scores for 209M: GIFT-Eval MASE 0.658, CRPS 0.446 (Chronos-2 0.698, 0.485); TIME MASE 0.626, CRPS 0.522 (Chronos-2 0.662, 0.556); fev-bench SQL skill 50.39, MASE skill 39.49 (Chronos-2 47.28, 35.50). Also ahead of t0-gamma, TimesFM-3 and Toto-2.0-2.5B on each. No explicit ranks, no energy-specific numbers.

title: LICENSE (Modified MIT), Timestral-209M
note: MIT-style grant over the weights with attribution, plus a revenue cap: an organisation whose global consolidated monthly revenue exceeded 20 million USD in the preceding month has no rights without a separate commercial licence from Mistral (or must use hosted services). Applies to derivatives too. No non-commercial clause; commercial use allowed below the cap.

title: Timestral (arXiv 2610.37585 v1, abstract page)
note: Tech report, v1 submitted 2026-10-27, cs.AI. Four probabilistic forecasting models (5M to 209M). Says they set a new state of the art on GIFT-Eval, TIME and fev-bench and that the 209M and 123M models take the top two places on every metric. Native known-future covariates in a causal architecture. Pretrained on synthetic data only, then post-trained on real plus synthetic data.

title: Timestral (arXiv 2610.37585 v1, full text)
note: Real post-training datasets are not named; no cutoff date and no statement on overlap with benchmark test sets. No with/without-covariate ablation: covariates are used where a task provides them. No energy-specific breakdown; IND-Eval (energy, manufacturing, transport) is aggregate only: nMASE 0.646, nCRPS 0.435 for 209M. Only named baseline is Seasonal Naive as normaliser. No coverage results.

title: Timestral (arXiv 2610.37585 v1, full text)
note: Cost notes: covariates raise inference latency to 1.7 to 2.0 times that of eight target variates; latency grows nearly in proportion to context beyond 2,048 steps. Benchmark horizons and test-window lengths were not found in the text as read.

title: Timestral: Mistral's time-series foundation models (blog)
note: Published 2026-10-15. Says the 209M model ranks first on GIFT-Eval, TIME and fev-bench among pretrained zero-shot models, single checkpoint, no ensembling; results submitted to the GIFT-Eval and TIME leaderboards. Says the 28M model beats Chronos-2 on GIFT-Eval and TIME. No electricity-load example; energy appears only as a customer category.

title: Timestral: Mistral's time-series foundation models (blog)
note: CPU claim: on a server CPU with 8 threads, a one-day-ahead forecast from three weeks of 15-minute history takes 113 ms with the 209M model and 17 ms with the 5M model; no GPU needed. Context 32,768 steps. Licence Modified MIT.

title: mistralai/timestral (GitHub)
note: Code under Apache 2.0, weights licensed separately. One commit on main, no releases or tags. forecast() takes known_covariates shaped (B, C_known, T + horizon) and past_covariates, plus categorical variants. Python >= 3.10, torch >= 2.4, no GPU needed. No load example and no benchmark reproduction scripts described in the README.
